name: GeoFidelity-Bench
description: GeoFidelity-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating whether text-to-image street-view generations match a target location at the level of named street blocks. Version 3.0.0 contains 112 named street blocks from 25 cities across six continents, 7,563 curated Mapillary reference images with GPS and capture metadata, 16,128 generated images from six open-source generators, prompt-control metadata, and evaluation outputs for geographic fidelity diagnostics.
rai:dataCollection: Reference panels were collected by querying named OpenStreetMap highway ways within 25 global cities, carving spatially separated named street blocks, downloading public Mapillary street-level images around each block, and retaining images that passed daylight, camera, OSM-buffer, urban-scene, semantic-ratio, image-quality, and manual-review filters. Generated panels were produced from the released prompt metadata using six open-source text-to-image models with deterministic seeds; the L0 city-only condition reuses images from an earlier city-only generation pool with the identical city/country prompt template.
rai:dataCollectionType: Generated images from open-source text-to-image models
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Coverage follows Mapillary contributor activity and OSM naming density. Some cities retain many curated blocks, while Berlin, Melbourne, and Nairobi retain one block each. Missing local hard negatives are explicitly represented by smaller retrieval galleries rather than filled with unreleased candidate blocks.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data consist of public Mapillary JPEG images, per-image GPS and capture metadata, OpenStreetMap way geometry and neighborhood labels, generated JPEG images, prompt manifests, and CSV/JSON evaluation outputs.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: No geographic, image, or metric values are imputed. Missing negative-panel candidates are left unavailable and evaluated with the available released candidates.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Remove panoramas, non-perspective cameras, night images, strong blur, extreme exposure, low colorfulness, and non-urban scenes.
Retain images within a 30 meter OSM buffer and apply fixed Mapillary-Vistas semantic-ratio gates for road, sky, building, vehicle, and urban content.
Run a manual keep/drop audit only for clear visual failures such as indoor views, private driveways, duplicated frames, or images where the street is not visible.
Generate model images with deterministic seeds from shared prompt templates for city-only, named-block, and GPS-augmented prompts.
rai:dataDataManipulationProtocol: The release preserves selected public reference images and generated images as JPEG files and stores metadata in JSON and CSV files. The benchmark does not alter source imagery beyond standard file storage and curation-based inclusion or exclusion.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Street block labels, city, country, driving side, way geometry, and neighborhood labels are derived from OpenStreetMap and nearby-place metadata.
Automatic image annotations include SigLIP urban-scene scores, Mapillary-Vistas semantic ratios, quality measures, and evaluation metrics.
Manual review records a binary keep/drop decision under a written visual-failure rubric.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Self-contained browser interface for the human-evaluation pilot
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The benchmark reports curation thresholds, city-level coverage, segmentation reliability checks, prompt-ablation uncertainty checks, and a small tie-aware human pilot.
The human pilot is treated as a perceptual sanity check and not as a metric-selection experiment.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each retained reference image has one block assignment and automatic curation annotations. Manual review is a single keep/drop audit for retained or rejected candidates. The human pilot contains one completed rating file covering 200 answered trials.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotator demographics are not collected for the manual curation audit or the released human pilot.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating geographic fidelity of text-to-image street-view generation.
Prompt-conditioning ablations for city-only, named-block, and GPS-augmented prompts.
Benchmarking model rankings and diagnostic metrics under matched block-level references.
Auditing whether generated street scenes reflect local visual evidence beyond generic city-level plausibility.
rai:dataBiases: Mapillary coverage is uneven across cities and neighborhoods because it depends on contributor activity, capture hardware, and local mapping practices.
OpenStreetMap naming density affects which streets can enter the named-block benchmark.
Daylight and camera filters bias the reference set toward daytime perspective street imagery.
Semantic and signage-sensitive filters may behave differently across scripts, urban forms, and low-resource regions.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark measures visual agreement with a reference panel, not factual identity of an exact street address.
The dataset is designed for matched model comparisons and prompt ablations, not for claiming that one city is intrinsically easier or harder without per-city coverage checks.
Text-only GPS prompts do not test coordinate-native generation systems that consume maps, trajectories, satellite images, layouts, or retrieved street-view evidence.

Reference images may include public street-level content and already-blurred bystanders or vehicles from Mapillary; the release is not intended for person identification, surveillance, or evidentiary use.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark can help measure and reduce stereotyped or geographically inaccurate depictions of places, but generated location imagery may mislead if presented as real evidence. Users should report results as local visual plausibility against a curated reference panel and avoid surveillance, re-identification, or claims that generated images depict real events.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark uses public Mapillary street-level imagery, which may contain already-blurred faces, license plates, storefronts, vehicles, and public-space context.
The dataset does not add person identity labels, face labels, license-plate labels, demographic labels, or private-address labels.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will maintain the benchmark release, curation pipeline, evaluation code, generated images, and metadata. Future extensions may add cities, generators, conditioning modes, or retuned curation thresholds; versioned releases should preserve the current v3.0.0 files for reproducibility.
